task: Find out which version of Node.js is the current LTS (long-term support) release, and get to the page where I can download it for Windows.
summary: The current LTS release is v26.13.0, announced clearly as the default value of combobox "Version" on the Download page. I reached the Windows downloads: choosing Windows in the custom "Operating System" list worked with a screen reader, and the page then offered "Windows Installer (.msi)" and "Standalone Binary (.zip)". Overall a good experience: skip link, landmarks, named controls. Minor issues: two drop-downs share the name "Operating System", the popup list and a code block have no name.

steps.reason: In the main navigation I hear link "Download"; it should lead to the download page.

issues.title: Two different drop-downs are both named "Operating System"
issues.description: The download page has two comboboxes called "Operating System" (one for the install command, one for prebuilt downloads), plus two called "Platform". In a list of form controls they sound identical, so it is not clear which one changes which download.
issues.fix: Give each control a distinct name, e.g. aria-label="Operating system for the install command" and aria-label="Operating system for the prebuilt download", or group each set in a <fieldset> with its own <legend>.

issues.title: Open option list has no name
issues.description: When I opened the "Operating System" drop-down, the list was announced as an unnamed listbox. The options themselves were clear, so it did not stop me.
issues.fix:
Link the popup list to its trigger label:
…

issues.title: Focusable code block has no name
issues.description: The command example is a focusable region announced only as an unnamed element, so a keyboard or screen reader user tabbing through the page hears a stop with no explanation.
